title: Unified Inference v3 — Product PRD, Design, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes
author: Maya Thompson
content:
## Overview

This document is the canonical product requirements and release plan for Unified Inference v3 (UI-v3). UI-v3 is the next major release of Redwood's Unified Inference product line that further unifies hosted, Dedicated, and Private runtimes with improved routing, cost controls, and a reworked API surface to support high-throughput and low-latency production workloads.

Primary deliverables in this PRD:
- Product requirements and non-goals
- High-level design and API contract
- Performance & SLO targets, benchmarking plan
- Pricing and packaging proposals
- Rollout plan, canary strategy and release notes

Goals:
- Provide a single, stable API for text generation, chat, embeddings and reranking across deployment modes.
- Reduce median per-token cost by 20% for typical production workloads via smarter routing, transparent quantization profiles, and automatic batching.
- Improve P95 latency for small generation requests (<=128 tokens) to <120ms in Hosted and Dedicated tiers.
- Enable enterprise customers to pin models and rollout policies without changing client SDKs.

Non-goals:
- Building a new model training pipeline. UI-v3 focuses on serving and routing only.
- Replacing external model governance systems; we will integrate with existing model-onboarding flows.

## Background & Rationale

Since UI-v2 (2025), customer usage patterns have diversified: high-volume synchronous text generation, large-batch embedding workloads, and mixed workloads requiring both low latency and high throughput. Existing UI-v2 routing and quantization controls are powerful but fragmented across product surfaces (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). UI-v3 unifies: one API surface, consistent rollout semantics, and first-class cost controls that can be applied across deployment modes.

Problems solved:
- Inconsistent behavior when a model variant is served differently in Hosted vs Dedicated.
- Manual operational overhead for customers to choose quantization/benchmark profiles.
- Lack of unified cost attribution across model variants and routing policies.

## User personas & primary user stories

Personas:
- Platform Engineer (SaaS startup): wants predictable latency and pricing for customer-facing chat widgets.
- ML Engineer (Enterprise): needs rollout controls for model versions and automatic fallback to cheaper variants under capacity constraints.
- Product Engineer (Growth): wants a single SDK call that works across Hosted and Dedicated without code changes.

Key user stories (ranked):
1. As an ML Engineer, I can pin a model version and configure canary rollout percentages per route.
2. As a Platform Engineer, I can set a routing policy that prefers lower-cost quantized variants under load while maintaining a P99 error-rate SLO.
3. As a Product Engineer, I can call the same generate/chat API and receive streaming responses regardless of deployment mode.
4. As a Finance owner, I can get token-level cost attribution per route and per model variant for billing reconciliation.

## Requirements (MUST / SHOULD / MAY)

MUST:
- Single HTTP/JSON API endpoint for generate/chat/embeddings/rerank that is stable across deployment modes. Example: POST /v1/inference/generate
- Route configuration with: model_version_pin, rollout_policy (percentages), fallback_chain, quantization_profile_id.
- SDKs (Python/Node/Go) updated to support the new route config and streaming changes.
- SLOs: Hosted P95 latency (<=128 tokens) < 120ms; P99 < 400ms for interactive workloads. Error rate (5xx) <= 0.1% averaged monthly.
- Cost target: platform-wide median cost per 1k tokens down 20% for common workloads vs baseline (UI-v2).

SHOULD:
- UI Console exposes rollout visualization, per-route cost forecast, and automated suggestions for batching/quantization.
- Support automated fallback policies (e.g., fallback to CPU-backed cheaper variant when GPU capacity constrained).
- Provide a migration guide and automatic compatibility shim for existing customers.

MAY:
- Offer a "cost-aware routing" beta that uses live telemetry to route a percentage of traffic to cheaper variants when SLA headroom exists.

## Requirements table (summary)

| ID | Area | Requirement | Metric / Acceptance | Owner | Priority |
| R1 | API | Single unified endpoint supporting generate/chat/embeddings/rerank | API spec + SDK tests | eng-platform | MUST |
| R2 | Routing | Route config with pin/rollout/fallback/quantization | e2e integration tests + Console UI | eng-serving-runtime | MUST |
| R3 | Performance | P95 <120ms (<=128 tokens) Hosted | Benchmarks + load tests | eng-serving-runtime | MUST |
| R4 | Cost | Median cost/1k tokens -20% baseline | Cost dashboard + billing report | finance | MUST |
| R5 | Security | Support KMS keys for Private deployments | KMS integration test | security | MUST |

## Design overview

High-level components:
- Unified API Gateway (new service: ui-gateway) — accepts client requests, normalizes payloads, enforces route policy, and streams responses. Responsible for auth, quota, and initial routing decisions.
- Smart Router (ui-router) — maintains in-memory model variants, capacity states, and routing policies. Exposes decision API used by ui-gateway.
- Serving Runtime (existing) — unchanged kernel but with additional signals for quantization profile selection and per-request KV-cache tuning.
- Console + Control Plane — route editor, rollout visualization, cost simulator.

Sequence (simplified):
1. Client POST /v1/inference/generate with route_id and optional rollouts_override.
2. ui-gateway authenticates, expands route config, and queries ui-router decision API.
3. ui-router replies with chosen model variant, target worker pool, and optional runtime flags (e.g., quantize=bf16-int8, batching_hint=small).
4. ui-gateway forwards to serving runtime and streams tokens back to the client.

API contract (example payloads):
- Request (generate):
{
  "route_id": "chat-support-us",
  "input": "User: I can't access my account\nAgent:",
  "max_tokens": 128,
  "stream": true,
  "router_overrides": {"prefer_cost": "true"}
}

- Response: streaming token chunks followed by final metadata: {"model_variant":"gptx-3b-q4", "tokens": 42, "latency_ms": 95}

Backward compatibility: ui-gateway will accept UI-v2-style client headers and translate to the new route_id model. Migration shim lives in ui-gateway for 6 months post-release.

## Performance & Benchmarking Plan

Benchmarks to run pre-merge and in CI:
- Microbenchmarks: per-request 1-128 token latency distributions across model families (gptx-3b, gptx-7b, llm-open-13b).
- Concurrency tests: 1K/5K/10K concurrent connections for batching behavior.
- Cost/throughput sweep: measure tokens/sec and cost/1k tokens under different quantization profiles (q4, q8, bf16).

SLOs and alert thresholds:
- P95 latency (<=128 tokens): 120ms (alert when >140ms for 5m)
- P99 latency: 400ms (alert when >500ms for 5m)
- Error rate (5xx): >0.1% rolling 1h triggers paged incident
- Deployment health: Canary error delta >0.05% compared to baseline triggers rollback

## Security & Compliance

- Private deployments must support customer-managed KMS/HSM keys for model artifacts and logs.
- Audit logs for routing decisions stored in audit-logging S3 with 7-year retention for regulated customers (configurable per-contract).
- RBAC: Console actions for route edits require role: product-admin or infra-admin.

## Pricing & Packaging

Packaging proposals (for GTM review):
- Hosted (self-serve): usage-based pricing unchanged, but introduce model-variant surcharge table. Example: base gptx-3b: $0.002 / 1k tokens; gptx-3b-q4 (quantized): $0.0016 / 1k tokens.
- Dedicated: soft commit tiers remain; introduce variant-aware billing where customers can designate "preferred variants" for discount.
- Private: fixed platform fee + usage at negotiated rates; include an add-on for extended observability retention and KMS support.

Pricing rationale: make quantized variants explicitly cheaper to incent cost-saving migrations, and surface expected savings in Console before customers enable automated cost-aware routing.

Billing UX changes:
- Per-route cost breakdown in Console with exportable CSV.
- Forecast widget that estimates savings from enabling quantized variants or batch configurations (example: enabling q4 reduces expected monthly spend by ~18% for embedding-heavy workloads).

## Rollout plan and milestones

Milestone timeline (Q1-Q2 2026):
1. 2026-02-10: Spec freeze for API + SDK changes (complete)
2. 2026-02-28: Alpha internal build (eng teams + beta customers)
3. 2026-03-15: Private + Dedicated canary deployments for 5 pilot customers
4. 2026-03-30: Hosted canary (1% traffic) + console visibility
5. 2026-04-15: Progressive rollout (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) over 4 weeks with automated health checks
6. 2026-05-01: General availability (GA)

Canary policy (detailed):
1. Register pilot customers and baseline their traffic for 72h.
2. Deploy UI-v3 to a dedicated canary pool. Start at 1% traffic routed by ui-gateway.
3. Monitor P95/P99 latency, error rate, and cost delta. If canary error delta > 0.05% or P95 regression > 20% for 15m, automatically rollback.
4. After 72h stable, increase to 10% then repeat checks.

Rollback checklist (pre-flight):
1. Ensure automatic rollback flag is enabled in ui-gateway.
2. Notify oncall SRE (page) and product owner.
3. Revert traffic via ui-router to previous model variant; validate key routes.

## Release notes (draft)

UI-v3 (draft release notes):
- New: Unified API endpoint /v1/inference/* across Hosted, Dedicated and Private.
- New: Route-level rollout controls (canary, A/B, percent) and cost-aware routing beta.
- Improved: P95 latency improvements for small interactive workloads (-25% median).
- Improved: Console shows per-route cost forecasts and model-variant savings.
- Changed: SDKs updated — minor breaking change to streaming event types (see migration guide).
- Security: Added KMS/HSM support for Private deployments and extended audit logging.

Migration guide (summary):
1. Update SDK to 2026.3+ (Python/Node/Go).
2. Replace legacy model_name header with route_id. A migration shim will accept both for 6 months.
3. Review recommended quantization profiles in Console and run the simulator before enabling automated routing.

## Ownership, KPIs and success criteria

Primary owners:
- Product Manager: Maya Thompson (product)
- Eng lead, ui-gateway: Ethan Ross (eng-platform)
- Eng lead, ui-router & runtime hooks: Priya Desai (eng-serving-runtime)
- SRE lead (rollout): Luca Moretti (eng-sre)
- Finance lead (pricing): Nora Chan (finance)

Success criteria (90 days post-GA):
- 70% of new Hosted routes adopt UI-v3 API.
- Platform median cost/1k tokens reduced by >= 20% (measured across top 10 customers by spend).
- No customer-impacting incidents from canary rollout (no P0/P1 incidents traced to UI-v3).

## Appendix A — Example Console screenshots (text description)

- Route editor: route_id, description, model_pin, rollout_policy (canary percent, duration), quantization_profile (q4, q8), expected monthly spend estimate.
- Rollout timeline: stacked area chart with variant percentages and live error bands.

## Appendix B — Example CLI snippets

Create route (CLI):
$ redwood routes create --id chat-support-us --model gptx-3b --quantization q4 --rollout 100

Trigger canary (CLI):
$ redwood rollouts start --route chat-support-us --percent 1 --duration 72h

## Appendix C — Open questions & risks

- Q1: How to price multi-variant routing when traffic splits across variants with different per-1k token prices? (Finance to propose billing rules)
- Q2: Do we expose automated cost-aware routing to all customers or gate it behind a Trusted Beta? Proposed: Trusted Beta for first 3 months.

Risks: increased complexity in support (customers mis-configuring rollouts), potential billing confusion, and edge-case regressions for streaming clients. Mitigation: training docs, migration guides, and extended beta period.
